question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=8y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-8x(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the general solution to the system of ODEs above?

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(8t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(8t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}].$*
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ of the system is given by

$$
{Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(8t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(8t)\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c \\  & ={e}^{At}\,c \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(8t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(8t)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(8t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(8t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(8t)\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.$
